 Marcos urges ASEAN, China to uphold peaceful dispute settlement
 by 
 Darryl John Esguerra
 Nov 16, 2026
 11:17 AM GMT+8
 ASEAN-CHINA TIES. President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. co-chairs the 29th ASEAN-China Summit on Monday (Nov. 16, 2026), along with Chinese Premier Li Qiang. China is among ASEAN's largest trading partners, with ties that span trade, investment and people-to-people exchange. (ASEAN PH 2026/PCO photo) 
 MANILA – President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Monday urged countries to translate their commitment to peaceful settlement of disputes into concrete actions, stressing the importance of self-restraint, mutual respect and practical cooperation amid regional tensions.
 Speaking at the 29th ASEAN-China Summit in Manila, Marcos said the 50th anniversary of the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia (TAC) offered an opportunity to reaffirm the region's commitment to international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes.
 “During this anniversary year, our shared commitment to international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes must be reflected in our actions, including through self-restraint, mutual respect, and practical cooperation,” he said.
 Marcos also cited progress in negotiations for a substantive and effective Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea, saying discussions had advanced based on the guidelines adopted in 2023.
 He reiterated that the proposed agreement must be consistent with international law, particularly the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).
 The Philippines, as chair of ASEAN for 2026, has been pushing for the early conclusion of COC negotiations to help manage disputes and prevent incidents in the contested waters from escalating.
 Negotiations, however, remain ongoing, with the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) saying the talks are about 80 percent complete.
 ASEAN-China ties 
 Marcos also highlighted the broader gains in ASEAN-China relations, which mark their 35th anniversary this year, along with the fifth anniversary of their comprehensive strategic partnership.
 He cited cooperation in trade, investment, energy security and environmental protection, including the joint statement on the regional impacts of developments in the Middle East and regional energy cooperation adopted in July.
 Chinese Premier Li Qiang, for his part, said two-way trade between China and ASEAN exceeded USD1 trillion last year, while cumulative two-way investment surpassed USD500 billion.
 Li also cited advances in cooperation in digital and green economies, artificial intelligence and regional connectivity.
 The Philippines continues to pursue economic engagement with China while broadening its security partnerships with other countries amid persistent tensions in the South China Sea. (PNA)
